stemMd: Each of the following salts is dissolved in pure water at 25 °C to make a 0.1 mol/L solution. Which solution has a pH greater than 7?
explanationMd:
Think of each salt as made from an acid and a base, and ask which parent is weak. The ion that comes from a **weak** parent reacts with water; the ion from a **strong** parent does not.

- NaCl: from NaOH (strong) and HCl (strong). Neither ion reacts: **neutral**, pH 7.
- $\mathrm{KNO_3}$: from KOH (strong) and $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ (strong): **neutral**.
- $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ and $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$: from the weak base $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and a strong acid. The ammonium ion gives $\mathrm{H^+}$ to water: **acidic**.
- $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$: from NaOH (strong) and acetic acid (weak). The acetate ion takes $\mathrm{H^+}$ from water:

$$\mathrm{CH_3COO^-} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{OH^-}$$

The extra $\mathrm{OH^-}$ makes the solution **basic**.

**Check:** strong acid with strong base gives neutral, strong acid with weak base gives acidic, weak acid with strong base gives basic; only sodium acetate fits the last pattern.

distractorRationale.b: Sodium chloride comes from a strong acid and a strong base. Neither ion reacts with water, so the solution is neutral.
distractorRationale.e: Potassium nitrate also comes from a strong base and a strong acid, so its solution is neutral, not basic.
distractorRationale.d: The ammonium ion is the conjugate acid of the weak base ammonia; it donates $\mathrm{H^+}$ to water, so the solution is acidic, pH below 7.
distractorRationale.a: Ammonium nitrate contains the ammonium ion, which makes the solution acidic; the nitrate ion, from a strong acid, does not offset it.

accessibilityText: A short text question. Each salt is dissolved in pure water at 25 degrees Celsius at 0.1 moles per litre, and the question asks which solution has a pH greater than 7. The choices are: sodium chloride, N a C l; potassium nitrate, K N O 3; ammonium chloride, N H 4 C l; sodium acetate, C H 3 C O O N a; ammonium nitrate, N H 4 N O 3.

provenance.notes: Original item. Tests predicting the acidity of salt solutions from the strength of the parent acid and base.

review.author: tolc-f-wave8-biochem-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Sodium acetate is the salt of a weak acid and a strong base; acetate hydrolyses to give OH-, so pH > 7. NaCl and KNO3 (strong acid + strong base) are neutral, and NH4NO3 and NH4Cl are acidic because NH4+ hydrolyses. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolcf-biochem-run1) reached the same answer: Acetate is the conjugate base of a weak acid and hydrolyses to give OH-, so sodium acetate solution has pH > 7. NH4NO3 and NH4Cl are acidic (NH4+ hydrolysis), while NaCl and KNO3 come from a strong acid and a strong base and are neutral.]
